title: Wave-particle duality
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:41Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: No bank point covers single photons and electrons building up a double slit pattern as evidence for wave-particle duality; the closest, Matter waves, covers de Broglie wavelength and electron diffraction, and Young's experiment only shows classical light interference, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Wave-particle duality
card: Light shows wave behaviour when it passes through two narrow slits. The waves overlap and make a pattern of bright and dark bands, called an interference pattern.
Light also shows particle behaviour. A detector can record a single photon arriving at one spot, not spread across the screen.
Send photons through the slits one at a time. Each one lands at a single point, but after many arrive the points build up the same bands as the wave pattern.
Electrons do the same. Single electrons build up a double slit pattern, so matter acts as both a particle and a wave. This is wave-particle duality.
draft.remember: Single photons and electrons land as points but build up a wave pattern, so both act as waves and particles.

a.q: Single electrons are fired at a double slit, one at a time. After thousands have landed, bright and dark bands appear. What does this show?
opts: Electrons act as both particles and waves
Electrons act only as particles, as each lands at a point
Electrons act only as waves, as bands form
Electrons must be interacting with each other
a.why: Each electron is detected at one point, which is particle behaviour, and the bands that build up are an interference pattern, which is wave behaviour. Electrons arriving one at a time cannot be interfering with each other, so that option is wrong.
a.clue: Think about both how each electron lands and what pattern forms.

b.q: In a double slit experiment, photons are sent through one at a time. A student watches the screen early on, when only a few photons have landed. What would the student see?
opts: A few separate points that do not yet show bands
A faint, smooth set of bands across the whole screen
One bright band at the centre of the screen
Nothing, as one photon cannot reach a screen
b.why: Each photon is detected at a single point, so early on there are just scattered dots. The bands only appear as many points build up. A smooth faint pattern would mean each photon spreads out when detected, which is not what happens.
b.clue: Each photon is detected at one spot, and the pattern takes time to build.

a.best: Electrons act as both particles and waves

b.best: A few separate points that do not yet show bands
